abrupt.ex: The meeting came to an abrupt end.

activity.en: the amount of work or business done

aggregate.en: total, made by adding all parts
aggregate.ex: The aggregate score decides the winner.

example.en: The aggregate figure hides big regional differences.
example.zh: 總計數字掩蓋了地區間的巨大差異。

note.meaning: 總計的、合計的；把各部分加總後的整體。
note.usage: 作形容詞放在名詞前（aggregate index / demand）；也可作名詞 in aggregate（總體而言）。常見於經濟、統計語境。

noteEn.meaning: total; made by adding all the parts together.
noteEn.usage: Used before a noun ('aggregate demand'); common in economics and statistics.

noteEs.exampleTr: La cifra agregada oculta grandes diferencias regionales.
noteEs.meaning: total; formado al sumar todas las partes.
noteEs.usage: Adjetivo antes del sustantivo (aggregate demand); común en economía y estadística.

noteHi.exampleTr: कुल आँकड़ा बड़े क्षेत्रीय अंतर छिपा देता है।
noteHi.meaning: सभी भागों को जोड़कर बना कुल।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले विशेषण (aggregate demand); अर्थशास्त्र व आँकड़ों में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 総計の数字は大きな地域差を隠している。
noteJa.meaning: 全体を合計した、総計の。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前で形容詞として使う（aggregate demand）。経済・統計の文脈で多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 총계 수치는 큰 지역 차이를 가린다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞 형용사로 쓰임(aggregate demand). 경제·통계에서 흔함.

ahead.ex: Busy weeks lie ahead for the team.
ahead.zh: 未來；之後（the year ahead：來年）

aib's.en: belonging to AIB, an Irish bank

ambition.en: a big aim you want to achieve
ambition.ex: The city's ambition is to plant a million trees.

as.en: in the role or way of

ascribed.ex: They ascribed the delay to bad weather.

associated.ex: Many health problems are associated with smoking.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attributed.ex: He attributed his success to hard work.
attributed.ja: 〜のせいにした（attribute A to B）

august.en: the eighth month of the year

back.en: to an earlier state or place
back.ex: The sun came back after the storm.

backed.ex: The plan is backed by local businesses.

bank.en: a business that keeps and lends money
bank.ex: I opened an account at a new bank.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

began.ex: The concert began at eight o'clock.

better.ex: Our team played better this week.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

big.ex: It was a big decision for the family.

billions.en: very large numbers; thousands of millions

bringing.en: causing something to reach a state
bringing.ex: The storm is bringing traffic to a standstill.
bringing.zh: 使（某事）（bring…to a halt：使突然停止）

broader.ex: We need to look at the broader picture.

builders.en: people or companies that build houses
builders.ex: The builders finished the new school in May.

building.en: the work of making houses or structures
building.ex: Building on the new road starts in June.
building.zh: 建築；建造（house building：住宅建設）

buoyant.ex: Sales remained buoyant over the summer.

example.en: The housing market remained buoyant despite higher interest rates.
example.zh: 儘管利率上升，房市依然暢旺。

note.meaning: （經濟、市場、需求）強勁的、蓬勃的；本義為「有浮力的」。
note.usage: 多用於商業語境：buoyant demand / market / sales；也可形容心情「愉快的」。

noteEn.meaning: strong and growing (about markets or demand).
noteEn.usage: Common in business: 'buoyant demand', 'a buoyant market'; it can also mean cheerful.

noteEs.exampleTr: El mercado inmobiliario siguió boyante pese a los tipos de interés más altos.
noteEs.usage: Común en negocios: buoyant demand/market; también significa animado.

noteHi.exampleTr: ऊँची ब्याज दरों के बावजूद आवास बाज़ार मज़बूत बना रहा।
noteHi.usage: व्यापार संदर्भ में: buoyant demand/market; मन के लिए "प्रसन्न"।

noteJa.exampleTr: 金利上昇にもかかわらず住宅市場は好調を維持した。
noteJa.meaning: （経済・需要が）好調な、活況の。
noteJa.usage: ビジネスで多用（buoyant demand / market）。気分が「明るい」の意味も。

noteKo.exampleTr: 금리 상승에도 주택 시장은 호조를 유지했다.
noteKo.usage: 비즈니스에서 자주 쓰임(buoyant demand/market). 기분이 "들뜬"의 뜻도 있다.

busy.ex: The city centre is very busy on Saturdays.

centres.en: large buildings or places for an activity
centres.ex: The town has two new sports centres.

challenge.en: a difficult problem to deal with
challenge.ex: Finding staff is a big challenge for shops.

changes.ex: The new law brought many changes.

civil.en: about public works like roads and bridges
civil.ex: She studied civil engineering at university.

closely.ex: Doctors are watching the patient closely.

come.ex: The news comes at a hard time for workers.

coming.ex: Plans for the coming week are ready.

commenced.ex: Work on the bridge commenced last spring.

example.en: Construction of the new hospital commenced in March.
example.zh: 新醫院的建設於三月開工。

note.meaning: 開始；commence 的過去式，比 begin/start 更正式。
note.usage: 可接名詞或 V-ing（commence work / commence building）；常見於公告、法律與新聞的正式文體。

noteEn.meaning: began; a more formal word than 'started'.
noteEn.usage: Used with a noun or -ing form ('commence work'); common in formal writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: La construcción del nuevo hospital comenzó en marzo.
noteEs.usage: Va con sustantivo o -ing (commence work); propio de textos formales.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए अस्पताल का निर्माण मार्च में शुरू हुआ।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा या V-ing के साथ: commence work; औपचारिक लेखन में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新病院の建設は3月に始まった。
noteJa.meaning: 始まった（begin より改まった語）。
noteJa.usage: 名詞や動名詞を取る（commence work）。公式文書やニュースで使う。

noteKo.usage: 명사나 동명사와 쓰임(commence work). 공식 문서·뉴스에서 사용.

commercial.en: related to business, shops and offices
commercial.ex: The building has commercial space downstairs.

compared.en: when you look at both together
compared.ex: Prices are high compared with last year.

component.en: one part of a larger whole
component.ex: Price is a key component of the decision.

confidence.en: a feeling that things will go well
confidence.ex: Business confidence rose in the spring.

confident.en: sure that things will go well
confident.ex: She is confident she will pass the exam.

conflict.ex: Many people left the region because of the conflict.

connected.ex: The delays are connected to the bad weather.

consecutive.en: following one after another without a break
consecutive.ex: It rained for five consecutive days.

example.en: The team has won four consecutive games.
example.zh: 這支球隊已連贏四場比賽。

note.usage: 常與序數詞或數字連用：for the second consecutive month / three consecutive years；同義於 in a row、successive。

noteEn.meaning: following one after another with no break.
noteEn.usage: Used with numbers: 'for the second consecutive month'; like 'in a row'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El equipo ha ganado cuatro partidos consecutivos.
noteEs.usage: Con números u ordinales: for the second consecutive month; equivale a in a row.

noteHi.exampleTr: टीम ने लगातार चार मैच जीते हैं।
noteHi.usage: संख्या के साथ: for the second consecutive month; समानार्थी in a row।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのチームは4試合連続で勝っている。
noteJa.usage: 数字や序数と使う（for the second consecutive month）。in a row と同義。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 팀은 네 경기 연속으로 이겼다.
noteKo.usage: 숫자·서수와 함께 쓰임(for the second consecutive month). in a row와 같은 뜻.

considerable.ex: The project cost a considerable amount of money.

constitute.ex: These delays constitute a serious problem.

construction.en: the building of houses or structures
construction.ex: Construction of the bridge began in May.

continue.ex: The rain will continue all day.

contracted.en: became smaller in size or activity
contracted.ex: The economy contracted by two per cent last year.

example.en: Car sales contracted sharply in the spring.
example.zh: 春季汽車銷量大幅萎縮。

note.meaning: （經濟、產業或數量）萎縮、縮小；contract 的過去式。
note.usage: 作「萎縮」解時為不及物動詞：The economy contracted by 2%. 注意 contract 也可指「簽約」或「感染（疾病）」。

noteEn.meaning: became smaller in size or activity.
noteEn.usage: Used without an object: 'The economy contracted by 2%.' 'Contract' can also mean to make a legal agreement.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las ventas de coches se contrajeron mucho en primavera.
noteEs.meaning: (la economía o un sector) se redujo; pasado de contract.
noteEs.usage: En este sentido es intransitivo: The economy contracted by 2%. Contract también significa contratar.

noteHi.exampleTr: वसंत में कार की बिक्री तेज़ी से घटी।
noteHi.meaning: (अर्थव्यवस्था या उद्योग) सिकुड़ गया; contract का भूतकाल।
noteHi.usage: इस अर्थ में अकर्मक क्रिया: The economy contracted by 2%. contract का अर्थ अनुबंध करना भी होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 春に自動車販売が大きく落ち込んだ。
noteJa.meaning: （経済・産業が）縮小した。contract の過去形。
noteJa.usage: この意味では自動詞：The economy contracted by 2%. contract には「契約する」の意味もある。

noteKo.usage: 이 뜻에서는 자동사: The economy contracted by 2%. contract는 "계약하다"라는 뜻도 있다.

contraction.en: a fall in size or activity
contraction.ex: The economy suffered a sharp contraction last year.

example.en: The factory sector stayed in contraction all year.
example.zh: 製造業整年都處於萎縮狀態。

note.meaning: （規模、數量或經濟活動的）萎縮、縮減。
note.usage: 常用於經濟、市場語境，如 economic contraction；在 PMI 中低於 50 即代表 contraction，反義為 expansion。

noteEn.meaning: a fall in size, amount or economic activity.
noteEn.usage: Common with economies and markets; the opposite is 'expansion'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El sector manufacturero siguió en contracción todo el año.
noteEs.meaning: reducción de tamaño, cantidad o actividad económica.
noteEs.usage: Común en economía (economic contraction); lo opuesto es expansion.

noteHi.exampleTr: कारखाना क्षेत्र पूरे साल संकुचन में रहा।
noteHi.meaning: आकार, मात्रा या आर्थिक गतिविधि में कमी।
noteHi.usage: अर्थव्यवस्था और बाज़ार के लिए प्रयोग; विपरीत शब्द expansion है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 製造業は一年中縮小が続いた。
noteJa.meaning: 規模・量・経済活動の縮小。
noteJa.usage: 経済や市場の文脈で多用。PMIでは50未満が contraction。反意語は expansion。

noteKo.exampleTr: 제조업은 일 년 내내 위축 상태였다.
noteKo.usage: 경제·시장 맥락에서 자주 쓰임. 반대말은 expansion.

contrast.en: a clear difference (by contrast: in comparison)
contrast.ex: By contrast, the north had a dry summer.

crept.ex: Prices crept up during the winter.

decline.en: a fall in amount or value
decline.ex: There has been a decline in bird numbers.

declined.en: went down in amount or value
declined.ex: Sales declined sharply in the winter.

delivering.en: providing or completing what was promised
delivering.ex: The company is delivering new trains next year.
delivering.ja: 実現すること；供給すること

demand.en: the need or wish for goods or services
demand.ex: There is high demand for new homes.

designed.ex: The course is designed for beginners.

did.ex: Our team did well in the final.

does.ex: He does his homework after dinner.
does.zh: 做；進行（does a survey：做調查）

down.ex: He sat down on the bench.

dropped.en: became lower in amount or value
dropped.ex: The temperature dropped quickly at night.

economist.en: an expert on money and trade

edged.ex: Share prices edged higher on Friday.
edged.zh: 緩慢移動；小幅回到（edge back into）

elevated.ex: Elevated food prices hurt poor families most.

example.en: Energy bills stayed elevated throughout the winter.
example.zh: 整個冬天能源帳單都居高不下。

note.meaning: （水準、數值）偏高的、高於正常的。
note.usage: 正式用語，常見於經濟、醫學：elevated prices / costs / risk / blood pressure；口語多用 high。

noteEn.usage: A formal word, e.g. 'elevated prices' or 'elevated risk'; in everyday speech say 'high'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las facturas de energía siguieron elevadas todo el invierno.
noteEs.usage: Término formal (elevated prices, elevated risk); en lenguaje coloquial se dice high.

noteHi.exampleTr: पूरी सर्दी बिजली-गैस के बिल ऊँचे रहे।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द: elevated prices/risk; बोलचाल में high।

noteJa.exampleTr: 冬の間ずっと光熱費は高止まりした。
noteJa.meaning: 通常より高い、高止まりした。
noteJa.usage: 硬い表現（elevated prices / risk）。日常では high を使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 겨울 내내 에너지 요금이 높은 수준을 유지했다.

elsewhere.es: en otros sectores; en otra parte
elsewhere.ex: Prices are lower elsewhere in the country.

employment.en: the number of people with jobs
employment.ex: Employment in the town rose last year.

encompasses.ex: The course encompasses art and history.

encompassing.ex: The park is huge, encompassing three lakes.

ending.ex: The goal ended his long losing run.

engineering.en: designing and building roads, bridges, machines

erupted.ex: Fighting erupted in the capital last night.

euro.en: the money used in Ireland and much of the EU
euro.ex: A coffee costs about three euro.

even.en: even as: at the same time as; although
even.ex: He kept working even as it got dark.

expansion.ex: The airport expansion will take two years.

expensive.ex: Rent in Dublin is very expensive.

factories.ex: The town has three car factories.

fall.en: a drop in amount or level
fall.ex: There was a fall in prices last week.

february.en: the second month of the year

fell.en: went down in amount or level
fell.ex: Sales fell by ten per cent.

figure.ex: The official figure shows rising unemployment.

findings.ex: The findings will be shared next month.

firms.ex: Tech firms are hiring more engineers.

forthcoming.ex: Tickets for the forthcoming tour sell fast.

example.en: Details will be announced in the forthcoming weeks.
example.zh: 詳情將在接下來幾週公布。

note.meaning: 即將到來的、即將發生的；也可指「（資訊、資金）可得到的」。
note.usage: 放在名詞前表「即將到來」：the forthcoming year / election；放在 be 後多表「主動提供的」，如 He was not forthcoming.

noteEn.usage: Before a noun it means 'coming soon'; after 'be' it can mean willing to give information.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los detalles se anunciarán en las próximas semanas.
noteEs.meaning: próximo; que va a ocurrir pronto.
noteEs.usage: Antes del sustantivo: the forthcoming election; tras be significa dispuesto a informar.

noteHi.exampleTr: विवरण आने वाले हफ़्तों में घोषित किए जाएँगे।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले: the forthcoming election; be के बाद अर्थ "सहयोगी, बताने को तैयार"।

noteJa.exampleTr: 詳細は今後数週間のうちに発表される。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前で「来たる」（the forthcoming election）。be の後では「協力的な、率直な」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 자세한 내용은 앞으로 몇 주 안에 발표될 것이다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에서 "다가오는"(the forthcoming election). be 뒤에서는 "선뜻 알려주는".

fuel.en: petrol, diesel, gas, etc. that make power
fuel.ex: Fuel prices went up again this week.

funded.en: paid for with money from someone
funded.ex: The study was funded by the university.
funded.zh: 資助的（publicly funded：公共資金資助的）

funding.ex: The school lost its government funding.

goal.ex: Her goal is to run a marathon.

got.ex: She got a good mark in maths.

government.en: the group of people who rule a country

grew.ex: The company grew quickly last year.

grow.en: to get bigger; to live as a plant
grow.ex: Ireland grows a lot of potatoes.

halt.ex: The strike brought the trains to a halt.
halt.zh: 停止（bring to a halt：使停止）

headline.en: main; the most important overall figure
headline.ex: The headline rate of inflation fell.

healthy.ex: The shop has a healthy number of customers.

heavily.ex: The town relies heavily on tourism.

help.ex: Volunteers help older people with shopping.

higher.ex: Prices are higher in the city.

hiring.ex: The bank stopped hiring this year.

homes.ex: Many students rent a room in a family home.

house.ex: They bought an old house by the sea.

however.ex: It was cold. However, we went out.

in.en: inside; at a time or place

increase.en: a rise in amount or number
increase.ex: There was an increase in rain this month.

increased.en: went up in number or amount

index.en: a number that measures change over time
index.ex: The price index rose last month.

indicate.en: to show or be a sign of

indicated.ex: Most students indicated a wish to study abroad.

indicating.ex: The results are positive, indicating real progress.

industry.ex: Tourism is a key industry in Kerry.

infrastructure.en: basic systems like power and roads
infrastructure.ex: The country must invest in infrastructure.

investment.en: money put in to get results

jobs.ex: The new factory will create 200 jobs.

key.ex: Trust is a key part of any friendship.

light.en: in light of: because of; considering
light.ex: In light of the rain, the game was cancelled.

likewise.ex: She left early, and likewise her brother.

linked.ex: Poor sleep is linked to stress.

managers.en: people who run part of a business
managers.ex: The managers met to discuss the budget.

marginal.ex: There was a marginal rise in prices.

measures.en: finds the size or amount of something
measures.ex: This test measures your reading speed.

modest.ex: The town saw a modest rise in visitors.

month.ex: I visit my grandmother once a month.

more.ex: We need more chairs for the guests.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: They opened a new shop in town.

nonetheless.ex: The task was hard; nonetheless, she finished it.

notched.ex: The team notched up its fifth win.

noted.ex: The teacher noted that homework was late.

example.en: Notwithstanding the bad weather, the match went ahead.
example.zh: 儘管天氣惡劣，比賽仍照常進行。

note.meaning: 儘管；雖然（= despite），屬正式用語。
note.usage: 可放在名詞前（notwithstanding the rain），也可放在名詞後（the rain notwithstanding）；多見於法律、報告等正式文體。

noteEn.meaning: despite; even though something is true (formal).
noteEn.usage: Can go before or after the noun; used in formal or legal writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: Pese al mal tiempo, el partido se jugó.
noteEs.usage: Puede ir antes o después del sustantivo; propio de textos formales o legales.

noteHi.exampleTr: खराब मौसम के बावजूद मैच हुआ।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले या बाद आ सकता है; औपचारिक लेखन में प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 悪天候にもかかわらず、試合は行われた。
noteJa.meaning: 〜にもかかわらず（改まった表現）。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前にも後にも置ける。法律文書や報告書などで使う。

noteKo.usage: 명사 앞이나 뒤에 올 수 있으며, 법률·보고서 등 격식 있는 글에 쓰인다.

number.en: an amount of things or people
number.ex: The number of visitors rose this year.

objective.ex: The main objective is to cut costs.

observed.ex: She observed that the room was cold.

offices.en: buildings or rooms where people work
offices.ex: The company moved to new offices.

orders.en: requests to buy goods or services
orders.ex: The shop received many orders online.

overall.ex: The overall cost was higher than planned.

performed.ex: The new shop performed well in its first year.

period.ex: He lived abroad for a short period.

persistent.ex: She had a persistent cough all winter.

example.en: Staff shortages remain a persistent problem for hospitals.
example.zh: 人手短缺仍是醫院長期存在的問題。

note.meaning: 持續的、揮之不去的（問題、狀況長期存在）。
note.usage: 常修飾負面事物：persistent problem / challenge / inflation；形容人時表示「堅持不懈的」。

noteEn.meaning: continuing for a long time and not going away.
noteEn.usage: Often used for problems ('a persistent problem'); for people it means not giving up.

noteEs.exampleTr: La falta de personal sigue siendo un problema persistente en los hospitales.
noteEs.meaning: que dura mucho tiempo y no desaparece.
noteEs.usage: Suele acompañar cosas negativas: persistent problem; para personas significa tenaz.

noteHi.exampleTr: कर्मचारियों की कमी अस्पतालों के लिए लगातार समस्या बनी हुई है।
noteHi.meaning: लंबे समय तक बना रहने वाला।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर नकारात्मक चीज़ों के साथ: persistent problem; व्यक्ति के लिए "दृढ़"।

noteJa.exampleTr: 人手不足は病院にとって根強い問題のままだ。
noteJa.meaning: 長く続く、なかなか消えない。
noteJa.usage: 否定的な事柄に多い（persistent problem）。人に使うと「粘り強い」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 인력 부족은 병원의 지속적인 문제로 남아 있다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 부정적인 것과 쓰임(persistent problem). 사람에게는 "끈질긴".

pick-up.ex: Shops reported a pick-up in sales.

pipeline.en: projects planned and waiting to start
pipeline.ex: The firm has many new products in the pipeline.
pipeline.ja: 案件の蓄積；パイプライン

pmi.en: purchasing managers' index; a business survey score

paragraphs: House building in Ireland went down in September. This is the second month in a row.
The bank AIB does a survey of the building industry every month. A score over 50 means growth. A score under 50 means less work. House building got a score of 47.2.
But other building work grew. Work on offices, shops and factories went up. Work on roads and other big projects also went up. The total score was 50.4.
Builders also got more new orders. But fuel is very expensive because of the war between the US and Iran. Builders still think they will be busy next year.
The Government wants 300,000 new homes by 2030.
House building in Ireland fell in September for the second month in a row, according to a monthly survey of the construction industry by AIB bank.

In the survey, a score above 50 means growth and a score below 50 means a fall. The score for house building dropped to 47.2. However, the total score for all construction was 50.4, which shows small growth compared with August.

Other types of building did better. Work on offices, shops and factories grew for the third month in a row, with a score of 52.4. Civil engineering, such as roads and other public projects, also started to grow again, at 52.3. New orders rose for the third month running, but the number of jobs fell slightly after ten months of growth.

Builders say demand is rising. However, high fuel prices, linked to the war between the US and Iran which started in February, are still a big problem. John Fahey, an economist at AIB, said builders remain confident about the next 12 months.
The Government wants 300,000 homes to be built by 2030, and it has promised billions of euro for infrastructure to help.

House building in Ireland contracted in September for the second consecutive month, even as the wider construction sector edged back into growth, according to AIB's monthly construction purchasing managers' index (PMI).

The index measures changes in activity, with readings above 50 indicating expansion and those below 50 signalling decline. The residential index slipped to 47.2, while the overall figure stood at 50.4, pointing to modest growth compared with August.

Commercial construction, which covers offices, factories and shopping centres, expanded for a third straight month, reaching 52.4. Civil engineering, including State-funded infrastructure, returned to growth at 52.3. New orders also increased for the third month in a row, although employment dipped, ending a ten-month run of hiring.

Firms linked the rise in activity to stronger demand, but higher fuel costs connected to the US-Iran war, which began in February, remain a key challenge. AIB senior economist John Fahey said builders' confidence about the year ahead remained resilient, supported by a healthy pipeline of projects.
The figures come as the Government pursues its target of 300,000 new homes by 2030, backed by billions of euro in infrastructure spending.

Residential construction in Ireland shrank for a second successive month in September, even as the broader building sector crept back into positive territory, AIB's monthly purchasing managers' index (PMI) reveals.
On the index, any reading above 50 denotes expansion and anything below it a contraction. House building sank to 47.2, whereas the headline figure of 50.4 indicated a marginal uptick on August.

Elsewhere, the picture was rosier. Commercial building – offices, factories and retail premises – notched up a third consecutive month of growth at 52.4, while civil engineering, encompassing State-backed infrastructure, rebounded to 52.3. New orders climbed for the third month running, although employment dipped, bringing a ten-month hiring streak to an abrupt halt.

Firms ascribed the pick-up to buoyant demand, yet soaring fuel costs stemming from the US-Iran conflict, which erupted in February, continue to weigh heavily on the industry. Nonetheless, AIB senior economist John Fahey noted that sentiment about the coming year remained resilient, underpinned by a robust pipeline of projects.
The figures will be scrutinised closely in light of the Government's goal of 300,000 homes by 2030, an ambition it has bolstered with billions of euro in infrastructure funding.

According to AIB's monthly construction purchasing managers' index (PMI), residential construction in Ireland declined for the second consecutive month in September, notwithstanding a marginal recovery in the sector as a whole.

The index is designed such that values above 50 represent expansion, whereas those below 50 indicate contraction. The residential component fell to 47.2; by contrast, the aggregate index reached 50.4, reflecting modest growth relative to August.

Other segments performed considerably better. Commercial construction expanded for a third successive month, registering 52.4, and civil engineering, which encompasses publicly funded infrastructure, returned to growth at 52.3. New orders likewise increased for the third consecutive month; employment, however, declined slightly, thereby ending a ten-month period of sustained recruitment.

Respondents attributed the increase in activity to rising demand. Nevertheless, elevated fuel costs associated with the US-Iran war, which commenced in February, constitute a persistent challenge. AIB senior economist John Fahey observed that confidence regarding the forthcoming year remained resilient, underpinned by a substantial pipeline of projects.
These findings are significant in light of the Government's objective of delivering 300,000 homes by 2030, a target supported by considerable investment in infrastructure.
